rules.title: Security deposit capped at 1.5 months' rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect a security deposit of more than 1.5 times one month's rent. Prepaid or advance rent, including last month's rent, counts toward this cap, so at move-in the landlord may collect no more than 2.5 months' rent in total (deposit plus first month). Any yearly increase in the deposit may not exceed 10% of the current deposit.
rules.key_value: 1.5x monthly rent; annual increase ≤10% of current deposit; ≤2.5x rent total at lease start
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals, including mobile homes.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings, unless the tenant sends a written request to apply the law (the law then applies 30 days later).
rules.quoted_span: one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less.

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant can opt in by written request)

rules.title: Deposit must be held in an interest-bearing account, with interest paid to the tenant and written notice
rules.requirement: The landlord must keep the deposit in an insured, interest-bearing account at a New Jersey institution and pay the interest to the tenant each year, either in cash or as a rent credit. Within 30 days of receiving the deposit, and each year after, the landlord must tell the tenant in writing where the deposit is held, how much it is, and the interest rate. If the landlord does not give notice or pay interest, the tenant can send written notice and apply the deposit plus 7% annual interest to rent.
rules.key_value: Interest goes to tenant annually; notice within 30 days; 7% per annum remedy
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law. Landlords holding deposits for 10 or more units may also use insured money market funds.
rules.exemptions: Seasonal rentals of 125 consecutive days or less (investment section only); owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.quoted_span: The interest or earnings paid on the security deposit belongs to the tenant and shall be paid
rules.penalty: Tenant may apply the deposit plus 7% annual interest to rent; misusing deposit money is a disorderly persons offense (fine of at least $200 and/or up to 30 days in jail, N.J.S.A. 46:8-25).

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant can opt in)

rules.title: Deposit must be returned within 30 days after tenancy ends
rules.requirement: Within 30 days after the tenancy ends, the landlord must return the deposit plus interest, minus itemized deductions for damage beyond normal wear and tear or other money owed. The return must go by personal delivery or by registered or certified mail. If the landlord wrongfully withholds it, the tenant may sue for double the amount withheld, plus court costs and attorney's fees.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rentals covered by the Security Deposit Law. If the tenant breaks the lease, the 30 days start when the unit is re-rented or the lease expires, whichever comes first.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings unless the tenant opts in.
rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongfully withheld, plus court costs and attorney's fees. If the tenant received government rental assistance, willful withholding carries a civil penalty of $500 to $2,000 per offense.

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant can opt in)

rules.title: Deposit must be returned within 5 business days after displacement by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation
rules.requirement: If a tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation and an official posts a no-occupancy notice or certifies that the displacement will last more than 7 days, the landlord must return the deposit within 5 business days. Within 3 business days of learning of the displacement, the landlord must tell the tenant where to collect it.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation where an official has barred occupancy or certified displacement of more than 7 days.

rules.title: Deposit return after lease termination for domestic violence
rules.requirement: If a tenant ends the lease early under the Safe Housing Act because of domestic violence, the landlord must make the deposit plus interest available within 15 business days. The landlord must tell the tenant in writing, within 3 business days, when and where to collect it, and must include an itemized list of interest and deductions.
rules.key_value: 15 business days; written notice within 3 business days
rules.coverage_conditions: Domestic violence victims who end their lease under the Safe Housing Act.

rules.title: No statewide rent control; increases must not be unconscionable and must follow local ordinances
rules.requirement: New Jersey has no statewide rent cap, but municipalities may adopt rent control. Any increase must not be unconscionable, must follow any local rent control ordinance, and may take effect only through a notice to quit and an offer of a new lease, never in the middle of a lease term. A tenant who believes an increase is unconscionable can challenge it before a local rent board or in court.
rules.key_value: No numeric state cap; unconscionability standard
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units are not covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.quoted_span: remain as long as they pay any legal increase in rent. The increase in rent must not be

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied two- or three-unit premises with two or fewer rental units

rules.conflict_note: This rule applies alongside local rent control rather than replacing it. Local ordinances (e.g. Jersey City, Hoboken, Newark) set the numeric caps where they exist.

rules.title: Newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt from local rent control for 30 years
rules.requirement: Newly built multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control ordinances for 30 years after construction is completed. Tenants should check with their local rent control board or municipal clerk to see whether their unit is covered.
rules.coverage_conditions: Newly constructed multiple dwellings, for 30 years after construction is completed.
rules.quoted_span: constructed multiple dwellings shall be exempt from any local rent control ordinances for a period
rules.conflict_note: This state law overrides municipal rent control (e.g. Jersey City, Hoboken, Newark) for buildings completed within the past 30 years. The guide does not give the statute's qualifying date or how 'completion' is defined. Units with HUD or NJHMFA subsidies may also be exempt from local rent control.

rules.title: No rent increases to cover costs of condominium or cooperative conversion
rules.requirement: When a building is converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership, the landlord may not raise rents to cover costs that result only from the conversion. Increases for new services or amenities are still allowed.
rules.coverage_conditions: All tenants in buildings being converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership.
rules.quoted_span: simple ownership of units, rents may not be increased to cover cos ts resulting solely from the

unresolvable_conditions: building is undergoing conversion to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership

rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act: good cause required to evict or refuse to renew
rules.requirement: A landlord may not evict a tenant or refuse to renew a lease, written or oral, without one of the good causes listed in the statute (such as nonpayment, disorderly conduct, damage, or lease violations after a notice to cease). Each cause requires a specific notice to quit, ranging from 3 days to 3 years. Self-help evictions are illegal.
rules.key_value: Enumerated good causes (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(a)-(r)), each with its own notice period
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals, including apartment buildings, single-family homes, mobile homes and rooming houses.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; transient or seasonal hotel and motel guests; units held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.
rules.quoted_span: No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a
rules.penalty: Treble damages plus attorney fees for false owner-occupancy claims or improper re-rental; civil penalty of up to $10,000 per violation for illegal residential use after a removal-from-market eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.6).

exemption_tests.description: Owner-occupied two- or three-unit premises with two or fewer rental units

rules.title: Relocation assistance for evictions to correct illegal occupancy
rules.requirement: A tenant evicted so the landlord can correct an illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance equal to six months' rent, paid by the landlord. If the tenant is not paid at least 5 days before removal, the tenant may be paid from a municipal relocation fund. Where no fund exists, unpaid amounts accrue 18% annual interest and become a lien on the property.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants evicted under N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(g)(3) to correct an illegal occupancy.
rules.quoted_span: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in
rules.penalty: 18% annual interest on unpaid relocation payments; the amount owed is a lien on the property.

rules.title: Law Against Discrimination bars refusing to rent based on source of lawful income
rules.requirement: A landlord may not refuse to rent to, or otherwise discriminate against, a tenant based on source of lawful income (such as housing vouchers) or other protected traits. Tenants can file complaints with the NJ Division of Civil Rights or in court.
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlord-tenant relationships, with limited exceptions.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two-family dwellings; rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home; single-sex residences.
rules.quoted_span: nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.penalty: Fines up to $10,000 for a first offense (N.J.S.A. 10:5-14.1a(a)), plus damages.

notes:
The source is the official NJ DCA 'Truth in Renting' guide, a secondary summary of state law. It gives no effective dates for any rule. Things left out on purpose:
- Application/screening fees: the guide only says landlords may charge the cost of the credit report and 'reasonable' application fees. That is no cap, so no fee record was made.
- Criminal history in screening: the guide does not mention the NJ Fair Chance in Housing Act, so no record was made.
- Out of scope: Truth in Renting Act distribution, habitability, late fees and grace periods, foreclosure notices, protected tenancy for condo conversions, and reprisal.
- Kept inside other records: the rule that advance rent counts toward the deposit cap (in the deposit-cap record), and the treble-damages owner-occupancy penalty (in the Anti-Eviction Act record).
- 30-year new-construction exemption (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5): flagged as preemption for NJ city rent control ordinances. The guide does not give the statute's qualifying date, so the coverage fields were left empty.
- Quote for the domestic-violence deposit record: the source text has a double space in 'lease  is', and the quote copies it exactly.
